simple.meaning: חֵדֶק (chêdeq) is a Hebrew word meaning “a prickly plant.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֵדֶק (H2312) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Proverbs 15:19, with occurrences in Proverbs, Micah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֵדֶק (H2312) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֵדֶק (H2312) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֵדֶק (chêdeq) / H2312 is traced through Proverbs 15:19, Micah 7:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2312. chedeq חֵ֑דֶק noun [masculine] brier (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic חִדְקָא Löw p. 147, No. 104 ; compare Arabic a kind of night-shade, see Lane 532 ); — כַּחֵדֶק טוֺבָם Micah 7:4 the best of them (si vera lectio) is like the brier (|| מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר ); חָ֑דֶק כִּמְשֻׂכַת עָצֵל דֶּרֶךְ Prov 15:19 the way of a sluggard is like a brier-hedge.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to sting;

occurrences.englishText: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch,
The best of them is like a brier.
